title: High-content analysis of neuronal morphology in human iPSC-derived neurons
protocol: Coat a black wall, clear flat-bottom 384-well plate suited for imaging using 50 μL geltrex coating solution (1:100 dilution in DMEM-F/12) per well.
Incubate the coated plates for 1 h at 37°C.
Apply 0.5 mL accutase® onto iPSC-derived neurons for 3 min at room temperature.
Transfer iPSC-derived neurons into a new plate containing culture medium.
Dilute accutase activity by adding 1 mL of culture media and washing off the cells.
Transfer the collected cells into a 15 mL falcon tube with 7.5 mL PBS for further dilution.
Wash the well with 1 mL of culture media, transferring any remaining cells to the same 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 100 × g, then remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the pelleted cells in maturation media.
Mix the cell suspension with maturation medium containing fresh DOX and 10 μM ROCK-inhibitor to a concentration of around 40,000 cells/mL.
Pipette 50 μL of the prepared cell suspension per well (384-well plate).
Incubate the cells in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Every second day, remove half of the culture medium and replace it with maturation medium containing fresh DOX.
Add 50 μL of the 8% PFA solution directly to the culture medium for a final 4% PFA solution.
Incubate for 15 min at RT under a fume hood.
Aspirate the culture medium / PFA solution and carefully wash each well three times with 50 μL PBS.
Leave 50 μL of 0.05% sodium azide in PBS in each well to improve conservation, or add the blocking solution for the subsequent staining steps.
If the cells will not be stained directly after fixation, seal the plate with parafilm and store it at 2°C–8°C.
Aspirate the PBS and add 50 μL of blocking solution to each well.
Incubate at RT for 1 h or overnight (12–24 h) at 2°C–8°C.
Prepare the primary antibody solution in blocking buffer by diluting SMI312 antibody 1:500 and MAP2 antibody 1:1000.
After incubation, aspirate the blocking solution and add 20 μL of primary antibody solution per well.
Seal the plate with parafilm and incubate overnight (12–24 h) at 2°C–8°C.
Aspirate the primary antibody solution and wash each well three times with 50 μL PBS.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution in blocking buffer including Hoechst 3342 by diluting both secondary antibodies 1:1000 and Hoechst 33342 1:2500.
Add 20 μL of secondary antibody solution per well.
Incubate in the dark at RT for at least 1 h.
Aspirate the secondary antibody solution and wash each well three times with 50 μL PBS.
Leave 80 μL of 0.05% sodium azide in PBS in each well after washing.
Seal the plate with parafilm.
Store the sealed plate at 2°C–8°C.
Check regularly for sufficient PBS in the wells to prevent drying out of fixed cells.
Set up the HCA platform and microscope settings.
Place the plate in the HCA imaging platform.
Select the appropriate plate format.
Choose the 20× Air, NA 0.4 objective.
Select non-confocal operational mode.
Define a binning of ‘1’.
Define the plate layout.
Select the wells and fields within each well for imaging.
Use the histogram on the image control panel to verify the maximum value.
Decrease exposure time or LED power if necessary to keep the maximum value below 60,000.
Acquire a z-stack by clicking ‘Test’ to determine the height of each channel.
Identify the sharpest focus for each channel and enter the respective height.
Go to ‘Run Experiment’, name it, and click ‘Start’.
Export the data as .tiff files after the run is finished.
Capture at least 12 fields of view per well to ensure robust data collection.
Imaging some wells with all 25 fields can help examine uniform cell growth throughout the well.
Include additional Z-planes if cells are not in focus, which increases acquisition time.
Set up the image acquisition based on a well containing control/untreated neurons.
Image the wells containing diseased/treated neurons before starting the analysis.
Process images from high-throughput experiments using CellProfiler for neurite outgrowth quantification.
Open the CellProfiler analysis pipeline.
Go to Images in CellProfiler.
Add images by dragging and dropping them into CellProfiler.
Go to Metadata in CellProfiler.
Enter the extraction method and metadata source.
Click on the magnifying glass to set an expression for interpreting metadata from file names or folders.
Update the text manually if necessary.
Click ‘Submit’ after entering or updating metadata settings.
Click ‘Update’ to extract and display the metadata in the CellProfiler window.
Go to NameAndTypes and adjust settings according to staining and image naming conventions.
Set channel 1 as Hoechst (nuclei), channel 2 as MAP2 (dendrites), and channel 3 as SMI312 (axons).
Select ‘File’ dropdown menu, then select ‘preferences’ in CellProfiler.
Select ‘Browse’ next to the ‘Default Output Folder’ and ‘Default Input Folder’.
Enter a filename for saving.
Go to the ExportToSpreadsheet Module at the end of the pipeline.
Enter a name at ‘filename prefix’.
Test the settings on multiple image sets using CellProfiler.
Click on ‘Start Test Mode’ in CellProfiler.
Go through each module using the ‘step’ button and adjust settings as needed.
Exit test mode by clicking ‘Exit Test Mode’ in CellProfiler.
Disable all windows and click the ‘Analyze Images’ button to start analysis.
CellProfiler will analyze image sets and export results to a spreadsheet on the selected drive and folder.
